::: {#exm-bayes-proportion-stan}
#### The Bernoulli model fitted with Stan

The data and the [uniform prior](bayesian-inference.qmd#def-flat-prior) are those of [the JAGS example](#exm-bayes-proportion).
The Stan program declares the data and the parameter with their types and ranges,
and the `model` block states the [prior](bayesian-inference.qmd#def-prior) and the [likelihood](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-lik):

```{r}
#| label: stan-proportion
#| code-fold: false
bernoulli_stan <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  array[N] int<lower=0, upper=1> y;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0, upper=1> p;
}
model {
  p ~ beta(1, 1);
  y ~ bernoulli(p);
}
"
stan_fit <- rstan::stan(
  model_code = bernoulli_stan,
  data = list(N = length(y), y = y),
  chains = 2,
  warmup = 1000,
  iter = 5000,
  seed = 1,
  refresh = 0
)
stan_draws <- as.matrix(stan_fit, pars = "p")[, "p"]
stan_summary <- rstan::summary(stan_fit, pars = "p")$summary
```

The table puts the two programs beside the $\operatorname{Beta}(56, 37)$ [posterior](bayesian-inference.qmd#def-posterior) of [the Beta-Bernoulli example](bayesian-inference.qmd#exm-beta-bernoulli):

```{r}
#| label: tbl-stan-jags-proportion
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior of the proportion from JAGS, Stan and the Beta posterior"
#| echo: false
summarize_draws <- function(draws) {
  c(
    mean = mean(draws),
    stats::quantile(draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
  )
}
beta_posterior <- c(
  mean = 56 / (56 + 37),
  stats::qbeta(c(0.025, 0.975), 56, 37)
)
comparison <- rbind(
  JAGS = summarize_draws(p_draws),
  Stan = summarize_draws(stan_draws),
  Beta = beta_posterior
)
knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 3, col.names = c("Mean", "2.5%", "97.5%"))
```

Stan's [potential scale reduction factor](mcmc.qmd#def-psrf) is
`r round(stan_summary[1, "Rhat"], 3)`,
and the sampler reports
`r rstan::get_num_divergent(stan_fit)`
divergent transitions.
Both programs reproduce the Beta posterior's mean and interval to about two decimal places.
The difference between them is in the model code, not in the answer:
the Stan program carries the types and ranges of its variables,
and it is compiled before it draws.
:::
